buyer_added_terms.text: 1. Generic OPTION CLAUSE: The Purchaser reserves the right to increase or decrease the quantity to be ordered up

to 25 percent of bid quantity at the time of placement of contract. The purchaser also reserves the right to increase the ordered quantity up to 25% of the contracted quantity during the currency of the contract at the contracted rates. The delivery period of quantity shall commence from the last date of original delivery order and in cases where option clause is exercised during the extended delivery period the additional time shall commence from the last date of extended delivery period. The additional delivery time shall be (Increased quantity ÷ Original quantity) × Original delivery period (in days), subject to minimum of 30 days. If the original delivery period is less than 30 days, the additional time equals the original delivery period. The Purchaser may extend this calculated delivery duration up to the original delivery period while exercising the option clause. Bidders must comply with these terms. 2. Buyer Added Bid Specific ATC Buyer Added text based ATC clauses 2.1. Bidder are advised to check application GST on their own before quoting. Buyer will not take any resp onsibility in this regards. GST reimbursement will be as per actuals or as per applicable rate (whichever is l ower), subject to the maximum of quoted GST%. 2.2. All firms are requested to participated in the bid as per the SCOPE OF REQUIREMENT. The same is atta ched under the "additional scope of work". Copy of SCOPE OF REQUIREMENT is to be uploaded back after e ndorsing authorised signatory and seal of the company/ firm as an indication of acceptance of the said SCO PE OF REQUIREMENT. 2.3. CERTIFICATES - UDYAM registration certificate 2.4. Bidders offer is liable to be rejected if they don't upload any of the certificates/ documents sought in t he bid documents, AT&C and corrigendum, if any. 2.5 Bidders shall submit the following documents along with their bid for vendor code creation: 2.5.1. Copy of canceled checque 2.5.2. Copy of PAN card 2.5.3.Copy of GSTIN 2.5.4. Copy of NEFT Mandate Duly Certified by bank. 2.6. Liquidated Damages (LD) clause will be imposed as per extant rules/ guidelines, is the supplier fails to supply the products within the delivery period. 2.7. Law. The Contract shall be considered and made in accordance with the laws of the Republic of India. The contract shall be governed by and interpreted in accordance with the laws of the Republic of India. 2.8. Arbitration. All disputes or differences arising out of or in connection with the Contract shall be settled by bilateral discussions. Any dispute, disagreement or question arising out of or relating to the Contract or relating to construction or performance, which cannot be settled amicably, may be resolved through arbitr ation. The standard clause of arbitration is as per Forms DPM-7, DPM-8 and DPM-9 (Available in MoD websi te and can be provided on request). 2.9. Penalty for use of Undue influence. The Seller undertakes that he has not given, offered or promised t o give, directly or indirectly, any gift, consideration, reward, commission, fees, brokerage or inducement to any person in service of the Buyer or otherwise in procuring the Contracts or forbearing to do or for having done or forborne to do any act in relation to the obtaining or execution of the present Contract or any othe r Contract with the Government of India for showing or forbearing to showfavour or disfavour to any perso n in relation to the present Contract or any other Contract with the Government of India. Any breach of the aforesaid undertaking by the Seller or anyone employed by him or acting on his behalf (whether with or wi thout the knowledge of the Seller) or the commission of any offers by the Seller or anyone employed by hi m or acting on his behalf, as defined in Chapter IX of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 or the Prevention of Corr uption Act, 1986 or of any other Actenacted for the prevention of corruption shall entitle the Buyer to canc el the contract and all or any other contracts with the Seller and recover from the Seller the amount of any loss arising from such cancellation. A decision of the Buyer of his representative to the effect that a breach of the undertaking had been committed shall be final and binding on the Seller. Giving or offering of any gi ft, bribe or inducement or any attempt at any such act on behalf of the Seller towards any officer/employe e of the Buyer or to any other person in a position to influence any officer employee of the Buyer for showi ng any favour in relation to this or any other contract, shall render the Seller to such liability/penalty as th e Buyer may deem proper, including but not limited to termination of the contract, imposition of penal dam ages, forfeiture of the Bank Guarantee and refund of the amounts paid by the Buyer. 2.10. Mandatory Clause 2.10. 1. Scope and completeness. The quantities shown are the estimated requirement for this

procurement. The bidder shall quote item-wise rates for every item in the prescribed unit of supply . Rates shall include packing, forwarding, freight, delivery, unloading and all applicable taxes/charges; GST shall be shown separately where the bid format requires it. No additional char ge shall be payable unless expressly permitted in the contract. 2.10. 2. Quality and conformity. All items shall be new, unused, genuine and of merchantable q uality, free from defects, damage, leakage, drying, fading, rust, deformation or other manufacturi ng/packing defects. Items shall conform to the description, size, grade, capacity, sheet count, pack size and other specifications stated in the Scope of Requirement. Where a brand/model is mention ed only for identification, equivalent or better products may be offered, subject to the stated specif ications and applicable procurement rules. 2.10. 3. Detailed specifications. The bidder shall clearly state the offered make/ brand, model ( where applicable), size, GSM, grade, pack contents, dimensions and other relevant specifications against each item. For paper products, the bidder shall state GSM, size and sheets per rim/pack as applicable. For pens/markers, the bidder shall state tip type/size and ink colour. For tapes, folders, envelopes and other size-sensitive items, the offered dimensions and material shall be specified. V ague entries such as “standard”, “assorted” or “as per requirement” without supporting particular s may be treated as incomplete. 2.10. 4. Sample evaluation. All bidders must submitted samples of all items within the tenderin g period for inspection by the technical evaluation board. Non-compliance with the same will make the bidder liable for rejection. 2.10. 5. Sample handling. Samples, where called for, shall be labelled with the bidder’s name, it em/serial number, make/brand and bid reference. The purchaser shall specify the submission deadline and delivery location in the request. Samples will ordinarily be returned after evaluation i f requested and practicable, except samples consumed or damaged during a disclosed test. Sampl e submission shall not be demanded indiscriminately for all items where documentary specificatio ns or catalogue evidence are sufficient. 2.10. 6. Printed Indian Navy file covers. For file covers requiring Indian Navy printing and lami nation, the successful bidder shall submit a proof/ sample for approval before bulk production. The approved artwork, wording, dimensions, paper/ card thickness, print clarity and lamination finish s hall be followed. Printing shall not commence until written approval is received. The bidder shall n ot reproduce or use any supplied emblem/ artwork for any purpose other than execution of this or der. 2.10. 7. Shelf life and consumables. Adhesives, correction pens, markers, pens, stamp-pad ink and similar consumables shall be within their manufacturer-declared shelf life at the time of delive ry and shall have adequate remaining usable life. Products shall be supplied in intact original pack aging with manufacturer identification and batch/date details wherever ordinarily provided. Dried- out, leaking, expired, refilled or counterfeit products shall not be accepted. 2.10. 8. Delivery and packaging. Delivery shall be made to the consignee/ location stated in the supply order within the delivery period specified therein. Items shall be packed to prevent damage , moisture, contamination and loss during transit. The bidder shall coordinate delivery with the con signee and provide a delivery challan showing item description, unit, quantity, make/brand and or der reference. Part delivery shall be permitted only with prior written approval. 2.10. 9. Inspection and acceptance. The consignee/ purchaser shall have the right to inspect a nd verify quantities, units, specifications, make/brand, packaging and quality at delivery and, wher e necessary, during the acceptance process. Receipt or payment shall not prevent rejection of late nt defects, short supply or non-conforming goods discovered subsequently within a reasonable ins pection period or applicable warranty/guarantee period. 2.10. 10. Rejection and replacement. Short-supplied, damaged, defective, counterfeit, expired, substandard or specification-deviating items may be rejected. The supplier shall, at its own cost, c ollect rejected goods and replace them with conforming goods within the period stipulated by the purchaser, without additional cost. If replacement is not made within the stipulated period, the pur chaser may take action as provided in the contract and applicable procurement rules. 2.10. 11. No unauthorised substitution. The supplier shall not change the approved make, bra nd, model, material, pack size or specification without prior written approval. Any approved substit ution must meet or exceed the tendered specification, must not increase the contract price, and m ust be documented before supply. 2.10. 12. Rate and unit clarity. Rates shall be quoted against the exact unit stated in the sched ule (Nos, Pkt, Sheets, Rim or Roll). The price of a packet/rim/roll shall include the stated number of sheets/metres or contents. Any discrepancy between the quoted unit and the required pack size s

hall be clarified during evaluation; the purchaser may reject an offer that cannot be evaluated on a like-for-like basis. 2.10. 13. Eligibility and fair competition. Eligibility requirements shall be limited to those nece ssary and proportionate to the value and nature of this supply. Bidders shall submit the document s specifically listed in the bid, such as PAN/ GST details where applicable, acceptance of tender ter ms, and declarations required by applicable rules. Do not impose an arbitrary turnover, prior-suppl y experience, local-office, or brand-authorisation condition unless justified by the procurement rule s and recorded requirement. Equivalent products meeting the stated specifications shall be consid ered. 2.10. 14. Evaluation and award. Bids shall be evaluated on the criteria and method stated in th e bid document. Where item-wise award, package-wise award or a single consolidated award is int ended, this shall be expressly stated before bidding. The purchaser reserves the right to seek clarif ications that do not permit a material change to the bid, and to reject non-responsive bids with rec orded reasons, in accordance with applicable rules. 2.10. 15. Integrity and authenticity. The supplier shall ensure that all goods are genuine and la wfully sourced. Counterfeit, refilled, duplicate or deceptively labelled goods shall be rejected. The bidder shall not offer inducements or engage in collusion, misrepresentation or other prohibited pr actices. Any applicable integrity, debarment and conflict-of-interest requirements under the gover ning procurement rules shall apply. 2.10. 16. Applicable rules and precedence. The procurement and resulting contract shall be g overned by the applicable Government of India procurement rules, GeM terms and conditions whe re procurement is through GeM, and the specific terms of the bid/supply order. In case of inconsist ency, the applicable statutory/procurement provisions and the order of precedence stated in the bi d shall prevail. 2.11. Agents / Agency Commission. The Seller confirms and declares to the Buyer that the Seller is the original manufacturer of the stores provider of the services referred to in this Contract and has not engaged any individual or firm, whether Indian or foreign whatsoever, to intercede, facilitate o r in any way to recommend to the Government of India or any of its functionaries, whether officiall y or unofficially, to the awardof the contract to the Seller; nor has any amount been paid, promise d or intended to be paid to any such individual or firm in respect of any such intercession, facilitati on or recommendation. The Seller agrees that if it is established at any time to the satisfaction of t he Buyer that the present declaration is in any way incorrect or if at a later stage it is discovered b y the Buyer that the Seller has engaged any such individual/firm, and paid or intended to pay any amount, gift, reward, fees, commission or consideration to such person, party, firm or institution, whether before or after the signing of this contract, the Seller will be liable to refund that amount t o the Buyer. The Seller will also be debarred from entering into any supply Contract with the Gover nment of India for a minimum period of five years. The Buyer will also have a right to consider can cellation of the Contract either wholly or in part, without any entitlement or compensation to the S eller who shall in such an event be liable to refund all payments made by the Buyerin terms of the Contract along with interest at the rate of 2% per annum above LIBOR rate. The Buyer will also ha ve the right to recover any such amount from any contracts concluded earlier with the Governmen t of India. 2.12. Access to Books of Accounts. In case it is found to the satisfaction of the Buyer that the Seller has en gaged an Agent or paid commission or influenced any person to obtain the contract as described in clause s relating to Agents/Agency Commission and penalty for use of undue influence, the Seller, on a specific re quest of the Buyer, shall provide necessary information/inspectionof the relevant financial documents infor mation. 2.13. Non-disclosure of Contract documents. Except with the written consent of the Buyer/Seller, other par ty shall not disclose the contract or any provision, specification, plan, design, pattern, sample or informatio n thereof to any third party. 2.14. Liquidated Damages. In the event of the Seller's failure to submit the Bonds, Guarantees and Docum ents, supply the stores/goods and conduct trials, installation of equipment, training, etc as specified in this contract, the Buyer may, at its discretion, withhold any payment until the completion of the contract. The Buyer may deduct from the CONTRACTOR as agreed, liquidated damages to the sum of 0.5% of the contra ct price of the delayed/undelivered stores/services mentioned above for every week of delay or part of a w eek, subject to the maximum value of the Liquidated Damages being not higher than 10% of the value of d elayed stores.

2.15. Notice. Any notice required or permitted by the contract shall be written in the English language and may be delivered personally or may be sent by FAX or registered prepaid/mail/airmail, addressed to the la st known address of the party to whom it is sent. 2.16. Transfer and Sub-letting. The Seller has no right to give, bargain, sell, assign or sublet or otherwise d ispose of the Contract or any part thereof, as well as to give or to let a third party take benefit or advantag e of the present Contract or any part thereof. 2.17. Taxes and Duties. 2.17.1 CONTRACTOR must indicate separately the relevant Taxes/ Duties likely to be paid in connection wi th delivery of completed goods specified in RFP. In absence of this, the total cost quoted by them in their b ids will be taken into account in the ranking of bids. 2.17.2. If CONTRACTOR is exempted from payment of any duty/tax upto any value of supplies from them, he should clearly state that no such duty/tax will be charged by them up to the limit of exemption which t hey may have. If any concession is available in regard to rate/ quantum of any duty/tax, it should be brou ghtout clearly. In such cases, relevant certificate will be issued by the Buyer later to enable the Seller to o btain exemptions from taxation authorities. 2.17.3. Any changes in levies, taxes and duties levied by Central/ State Local governments such as Goods & Services Tax (GST) on final product up ward as a result of any statutory variation taking place within con tract period shall be allowed reimbursement by the Buyer, to the extent of actual quantum of such duty/ta x paid by the Seller. Similarly, in case of downward revision in any such duty/tax, the actual quantum of re duction of such duty/tax shall be reimbursed to the Buyer by the Seller. All such adjustments shall include all reliefs, exemptions, rebates, concession, etc. if any, obtained by the Seller. Section 64-A of Sales of Goo ds Act will be relevant in this situation. 2.17.4. Levies, taxes and duties levied by Central/Sate/ Local governments such as Goods & Services Tax ( GST) on final product will be paid by the Buyer and they may not be indicated separately in the bid. CONT RACTOR is required to include the same in the pricing of their product. 2.18. Payment Terms. Payment through NEFT/RTGs will be made by AAO (Ezhimala) on submission of thed uty pre-receipted and stamped bill. 2.19. Advanced Payment. NO advanced payment will be made to contractor In any stage. All the payment s will be done only after duly submission of work completion certificate from contractor, joint inspection an d buyers inspection. On completion of inspection, buyer issues a satisfactory certificate and payment will b e done thereafter. 2.20. Force Majeure Clause. Neither party shall bear responsibility for the complete or partial nonperforma nce of any of its obligations (except for failure to pay any sum which has become due on account of receip t of goods under the provisions of the present contract), if the non performance results from such Force Ma jeure circumstances as Flood, Fire, Earth Quake and other acts of God as well as War, Military operations, blockade, Acts or Actions of State Authorities or any other circumstances beyond the parties control that h ave arisen after the conclusion of the present contract. .

1. Generic OPTION CLAUSE: The Purchaser reserves the right to increase or decrease the quantity to be ordered up

to 25 percent of bid quantity at the time of placement of contract. The purchaser also reserves the right to increase the ordered quantity up to 25% of the contracted quantity during the currency of the contract at the contracted rates. The delivery period of quantity shall commence from the last date of original delivery order and in cases where option clause is exercised during the extended delivery period the additional time shall commence from the last date of extended delivery period. The additional delivery time shall be (Increased quantity ÷ Original quantity) × Original delivery period (in days), subject to minimum of 30 days. If the original delivery period is less than 30 days, the additional time equals the original delivery period. The Purchaser may extend this calculated delivery duration up to the original delivery period while exercising the option clause. Bidders must comply with these terms. 2. The Contract shall be considered and made in accordance with the laws of the Republic of India. The contract shall be governed by and interpreted in accordance with the laws of the Republic of India. 2.8. Arbitration. All disputes or differences arising out of or in connection with the Contract shall be settled by bilateral discussions. Any dispute, disagreement or question arising out of or relating to the Contract or relating to construction or performance, which cannot be settled amicably, may be resolved through arbitr ation. The standard clause of arbitration is as per Forms DPM-7, DPM-8 and DPM-9 (Available in MoD websi te and can be provided on request). 2.9. Penalty for use of Undue influence. The Seller undertakes that he has not given, offered or promised t o give, directly or indirectly, any gift, consideration, reward, commission, fees, brokerage or inducement to any person in service of the Buyer or otherwise in procuring the Contracts or forbearing to do or for having done or forborne to do any act in relation to the obtaining or execution of the present Contract or any othe r Contract with the Government of India for showing or forbearing to showfavour or disfavour to any perso n in relation to the present Contract or any other Contract with the Government of India. Any breach of the aforesaid undertaking by the Seller or anyone employed by him or acting on his behalf (whether with or wi thout the knowledge of the Seller) or the commission of any offers by the Seller or anyone employed by hi m or acting on his behalf, as defined in Chapter IX of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 or the Prevention of Corr uption Act, 1986 or of any other Actenacted for the prevention of corruption shall entitle the Buyer to canc el the contract and all or any other contracts with the Seller and recover from the Seller the amount of any loss arising from such cancellation. A decision of the Buyer of his representative to the effect that a breach of the undertaking had been committed shall be final and binding on the Seller. Giving or offering of any gi ft, bribe or inducement or any attempt at any such act on behalf of the Seller towards any officer/employe e of the Buyer or to any other person in a position to influence any officer employee of the Buyer for showi ng any favour in relation to this or any other contract, shall render the Seller to such liability/penalty as th e Buyer may deem proper, including but not limited to termination of the contract, imposition of penal dam ages, forfeiture of the Bank Guarantee and refund of the amounts paid by the Buyer. 2.10. Mandatory Clause 2.10. 1. Scope and completeness. The quantities shown are the estimated requirement for this

procurement. The bidder shall quote item-wise rates for every item in the prescribed unit of supply . Rates shall include packing, forwarding, freight, delivery, unloading and all applicable taxes/charges; GST shall be shown separately where the bid format requires it. No additional char ge shall be payable unless expressly permitted in the contract. 2.10. 2. Quality and conformity. All items shall be new, unused, genuine and of merchantable q uality, free from defects, damage, leakage, drying, fading, rust, deformation or other manufacturi ng/packing defects. Items shall conform to the description, size, grade, capacity, sheet count, pack size and other specifications stated in the Scope of Requirement. Where a brand/model is mention ed only for identification, equivalent or better products may be offered, subject to the stated specif ications and applicable procurement rules. 2.10. 3. Detailed specifications. The bidder shall clearly state the offered make/ brand, model ( where applicable), size, GSM, grade, pack contents, dimensions and other relevant specifications against each item. For paper products, the bidder shall state GSM, size and sheets per rim/pack as applicable. For pens/markers, the bidder shall state tip type/size and ink colour. For tapes, folders, envelopes and other size-sensitive items, the offered dimensions and material shall be specified. V ague entries such as “standard”, “assorted” or “as per requirement” without supporting particular s may be treated as incomplete. 2.10. 4. Sample evaluation. All bidders must submitted samples of all items within the tenderin g period for inspection by the technical evaluation board. Non-compliance with the same will make the bidder liable for rejection. 2.10. 5. Sample handling. Samples, where called for, shall be labelled with the bidder’s name, it em/serial number, make/brand and bid reference. The purchaser shall specify the submission deadline and delivery location in the request. Samples will ordinarily be returned after evaluation i f requested and practicable, except samples consumed or damaged during a disclosed test. Sampl e submission shall not be demanded indiscriminately for all items where documentary specificatio ns or catalogue evidence are sufficient. 2.10. 6. Printed Indian Navy file covers. For file covers requiring Indian Navy printing and lami nation, the successful bidder shall submit a proof/ sample for approval before bulk production. The approved artwork, wording, dimensions, paper/ card thickness, print clarity and lamination finish s hall be followed. Printing shall not commence until written approval is received. The bidder shall n ot reproduce or use any supplied emblem/ artwork for any purpose other than execution of this or der. 2.10. 7. Shelf life and consumables. Adhesives, correction pens, markers, pens, stamp-pad ink and similar consumables shall be within their manufacturer-declared shelf life at the time of delive ry and shall have adequate remaining usable life. Products shall be supplied in intact original pack aging with manufacturer identification and batch/date details wherever ordinarily provided. Dried- out, leaking, expired, refilled or counterfeit products shall not be accepted. 2.10. 8. Delivery and packaging. Delivery shall be made to the consignee/ location stated in the supply order within the delivery period specified therein. Items shall be packed to prevent damage , moisture, contamination and loss during transit. The bidder shall coordinate delivery with the con signee and provide a delivery challan showing item description, unit, quantity, make/brand and or der reference. Part delivery shall be permitted only with prior written approval. 2.10. 9. Inspection and acceptance. The consignee/ purchaser shall have the right to inspect a nd verify quantities, units, specifications, make/brand, packaging and quality at delivery and, wher e necessary, during the acceptance process. Receipt or payment shall not prevent rejection of late nt defects, short supply or non-conforming goods discovered subsequently within a reasonable ins pection period or applicable warranty/guarantee period. 2.10. 10. Rejection and replacement. Short-supplied, damaged, defective, counterfeit, expired, substandard or specification-deviating items may be rejected. The supplier shall, at its own cost, c ollect rejected goods and replace them with conforming goods within the period stipulated by the purchaser, without additional cost. If replacement is not made within the stipulated period, the pur chaser may take action as provided in the contract and applicable procurement rules. 2.10. 11. No unauthorised substitution. The supplier shall not change the approved make, bra nd, model, material, pack size or specification without prior written approval. Any approved substit ution must meet or exceed the tendered specification, must not increase the contract price, and m ust be documented before supply. 2.10. 12. Rate and unit clarity. Rates shall be quoted against the exact unit stated in the sched ule (Nos, Pkt, Sheets, Rim or Roll). The price of a packet/rim/roll shall include the stated number of sheets/metres or contents. Any discrepancy between the quoted unit and the required pack size s

hall be clarified during evaluation; the purchaser may reject an offer that cannot be evaluated on a like-for-like basis. 2.10. 13. Eligibility and fair competition. Eligibility requirements shall be limited to those nece ssary and proportionate to the value and nature of this supply. Bidders shall submit the document s specifically listed in the bid, such as PAN/ GST details where applicable, acceptance of tender ter ms, and declarations required by applicable rules. Do not impose an arbitrary turnover, prior-suppl y experience, local-office, or brand-authorisation condition unless justified by the procurement rule s and recorded requirement. Equivalent products meeting the stated specifications shall be consid ered. 2.10. 14. Evaluation and award. Bids shall be evaluated on the criteria and method stated in th e bid document. Where item-wise award, package-wise award or a single consolidated award is int ended, this shall be expressly stated before bidding. The purchaser reserves the right to seek clarif ications that do not permit a material change to the bid, and to reject non-responsive bids with rec orded reasons, in accordance with applicable rules. 2.10. 15. Integrity and authenticity. The supplier shall ensure that all goods are genuine and la wfully sourced. Counterfeit, refilled, duplicate or deceptively labelled goods shall be rejected. The bidder shall not offer inducements or engage in collusion, misrepresentation or other prohibited pr actices. Any applicable integrity, debarment and conflict-of-interest requirements under the gover ning procurement rules shall apply. 2.10. 16. Applicable rules and precedence. The procurement and resulting contract shall be g overned by the applicable Government of India procurement rules, GeM terms and conditions whe re procurement is through GeM, and the specific terms of the bid/supply order. In case of inconsist ency, the applicable statutory/procurement provisions and the order of precedence stated in the bi d shall prevail. 2.11. Agents / Agency Commission. The Seller confirms and declares to the Buyer that the Seller is the original manufacturer of the stores provider of the services referred to in this Contract and has not engaged any individual or firm, whether Indian or foreign whatsoever, to intercede, facilitate o r in any way to recommend to the Government of India or any of its functionaries, whether officiall y or unofficially, to the awardof the contract to the Seller; nor has any amount been paid, promise d or intended to be paid to any such individual or firm in respect of any such intercession, facilitati on or recommendation. The Seller agrees that if it is established at any time to the satisfaction of t he Buyer that the present declaration is in any way incorrect or if at a later stage it is discovered b y the Buyer that the Seller has engaged any such individual/firm, and paid or intended to pay any amount, gift, reward, fees, commission or consideration to such person, party, firm or institution, whether before or after the signing of this contract, the Seller will be liable to refund that amount t o the Buyer. The Seller will also be debarred from entering into any supply Contract with the Gover nment of India for a minimum period of five years. The Buyer will also have a right to consider can cellation of the Contract either wholly or in part, without any entitlement or compensation to the S eller who shall in such an event be liable to refund all payments made by the Buyerin terms of the Contract along with interest at the rate of 2% per annum above LIBOR rate. The Buyer will also ha ve the right to recover any such amount from any contracts concluded earlier with the Governmen t of India. 2.12. Access to Books of Accounts. In case it is found to the satisfaction of the Buyer that the Seller has en gaged an Agent or paid commission or influenced any person to obtain the contract as described in clause s relating to Agents/Agency Commission and penalty for use of undue influence, the Seller, on a specific re quest of the Buyer, shall provide necessary information/inspectionof the relevant financial documents infor mation. 2.13. Non-disclosure of Contract documents. Except with the written consent of the Buyer/Seller, other par ty shall not disclose the contract or any provision, specification, plan, design, pattern, sample or informatio n thereof to any third party. 2.14. Liquidated Damages. In the event of the Seller's failure to submit the Bonds, Guarantees and Docum ents, supply the stores/goods and conduct trials, installation of equipment, training, etc as specified in this contract, the Buyer may, at its discretion, withhold any payment until the completion of the contract. The Buyer may deduct from the CONTRACTOR as agreed, liquidated damages to the sum of 0.5% of the contra ct price of the delayed/undelivered stores/services mentioned above for every week of delay or part of a w eek, subject to the maximum value of the Liquidated Damages being not higher than 10% of the value of d elayed stores.

Any notice required or permitted by the contract shall be written in the English language and may be delivered personally or may be sent by FAX or registered prepaid/mail/airmail, addressed to the la st known address of the party to whom it is sent. 2.16. Transfer and Sub-letting. The Seller has no right to give, bargain, sell, assign or sublet or otherwise d ispose of the Contract or any part thereof, as well as to give or to let a third party take benefit or advantag e of the present Contract or any part thereof. 2.17. If any concession is available in regard to rate/ quantum of any duty/tax, it should be brou ghtout clearly. Any changes in levies, taxes and duties levied by Central/ State Local governments such as Goods & Services Tax (GST) on final product up ward as a result of any statutory variation taking place within con tract period shall be allowed reimbursement by the Buyer, to the extent of actual quantum of such duty/ta x paid by the Seller. All the payment s will be done only after duly submission of work completion certificate from contractor, joint inspection an d buyers inspection. On completion of inspection, buyer issues a satisfactory certificate and payment will b e done thereafter. 2.20. Force Majeure Clause. Neither party shall bear responsibility for the complete or partial nonperforma nce of any of its obligations (except for failure to pay any sum which has become due on account of receip t of goods under the provisions of the present contract), if the non performance results from such Force Ma jeure circumstances as Flood, Fire, Earth Quake and other acts of God as well as War, Military operations, blockade, Acts or Actions of State Authorities or any other circumstances beyond the parties control that h ave arisen after the conclusion of the present contract. .
